21:23 Local Time, 16:23 GMT, 21:53 IST: This is a good fighting win for Pakistan and a hurting loss for Sri Lanka. This will definitely sting the Lankans. Coach Gary was so animated because his boys made a brilliant recovery. In fact, they were cruising to victory, until they threw the towel in in a mad last 30 minutes or so. Pakistan had it in full control for a good part early in this chase. Sri Lanka were 91/4 in the 20th over. Kamindu threw it away after getting a solid base. But then Janith walked in determined. With him came dew and he instilled belief into Pavan Rathnayake as well. The duo slowly dug in and the dew increased they knew batting was going to get easier. The partnership flourished to 119 runs. Shanaka walked in and played attacking cricket. He raced to 25 off 14 balls and that meant only 58 runs were needed off the last 8 overs.

Pakistan could not stem the flow, could not break the partnership. But then came the sudden shock from Sri Lanka. Both set batters Janith and Shanaka holed out in the space of 4 balls and coach Gary Kirsten was left fuming at the mindlessness in the middle. With enough time left, why will you give your wicket to Shaheen, who was finishing his spell he asked, pointing both fingers to the brain, pleading to use it better! Pakistan sniffed blood and they killed the game right there. Sri Lanka had very little resistance with the tail and Pakistan wiped out the last 5 wickets for just 15 runs. From 58 needed off 48 with 5 wickets in hand, Sri Lanka went on to lose by 37 runs! Pakistan holding their nerve under pressure, Sri Lanka throwing the game from the bag. That's the story for you.

Kusal Mendis | Sri Lanka captain: (Pakistan got 305. What did you make of that total? Did you think it was par?) I think we had to play a little bit more positively in the powerplay. Those guys (Pakistan) batted really well. Then I think the runs were enough. Our bowlers bowled really well in the last ten overs. The bowling unit did really well. I think myself.. I took a few more dot balls in the powerplay. That's why we struggled a little bit in the powerplay. (But that middle order must have given you a lot of hope, when Liyanage and Rathnayake were batting) Yeah, of course. Janith and Rathnayake batted really well, and Kamindu Mendis batted really well in the powerplay. I think only a couple of guys didn't score runs, and we made a small mistake after the 40th over. But we have to learn a couple of things and be ready for the next match.

So then! We had a spicy game today. Both teams had their noses ahead and one team completely threw it away. Both teams lost early wickets. Both had a good middle phase with the bat and both had collapses at the end overs. But in the end. Pakistan hung in there tight, kept wiping that wet ball and did not lose hope. The moment Sri Lanka blinked, they grabbed the game. Next up is Pakistan v England at the same venue. It could well be another exciting game folks. Can't wait for Tuesday! See you soon!
